1.1 **The Buyer:** Lagos Kitchen Collective, a business name registered with the Corporate Affairs Commission of Nigeria under registration number RC 1482293, with its registered address at 14 Adeola Odeku Street, Victoria Island, Lagos.

1.3 **Contact Persons.** For all matters arising under this Agreement, the Parties designate the following contact persons:

(a) For the Buyer: Mrs. Folake Adeyemi, Head of Procurement, email: folake.adeyemi@lagoskitchencollective.ng, telephone: +234 803 555 0192.

(b) For the Supplier: Mr. Ibrahim Musa, Accounts Manager, email: i.musa@nordicfresh.ng, telephone: +234 802 344 7810.

1.4 **Notices.** Any notice required or permitted under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly served if delivered personally, sent by registered post, or sent by electronic mail to the addresses set out above. Notices sent by post shall be deemed received seven (7) working days after posting. Notices sent by electronic mail shall be deemed received on the next working day after transmission, provided no delivery failure notification is received.

**2. COMMENCEMENT**

2.1 **Commencement Date.** This Agreement shall commence on the 1st day of March, 2024 (the "Commencement Date"). The Supply Contract LKC-2024-018 records its start_date as 2024-03-01, and this date is the effective date from which the Supplier's obligations to supply goods and the Buyer's obligations to pay for those goods shall take effect.

The Supply Contract LKC-2024-018 records its start_date as 2024-03-01. Record status: current.

2.2 **Initial Term.** The Agreement shall remain in force for an initial period beginning on the Commencement Date and continuing thereafter. The Parties acknowledge that the duration of this Agreement and any renewal options are addressed in Clause 3 (Term and Renewal) of this Agreement.

2.3 **Operational Readiness.** The Supplier confirms that, as at the Commencement Date, it holds all necessary permits, health and safety certifications, and food handling licenses required under the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) regulations and the Lagos State Ministry of Health guidelines for the supply of food products. The Supplier shall, upon request, provide copies of such certifications to the Buyer.

2.4 **Commencement of Deliveries.** The Supplier shall begin scheduling deliveries in accordance with the delivery schedule to be agreed upon in writing by the Parties within seven (7) working days following the Commencement Date. Pending the agreement of such schedule, the Supplier shall honour any purchase orders submitted by the Buyer in accordance with the ordering procedures set out in this Agreement.

**3. PURPOSE AND SCOPE**

3.1 The purpose of this Agreement is to establish a framework under which the Supplier shall supply the Buyer with the goods set out in Schedule A (the "Goods"), which schedule may be amended from time to time by written agreement of the Parties.

3.2 The Goods shall include, but not be limited to: fresh vegetables (including tomatoes, peppers, onions, leafy greens), fruits, poultry (whole and portioned), fish (fresh and frozen), dry goods (rice, beans, flour, pasta), cooking oils, spices, and other consumables required for the Buyer's kitchen operations.

3.3 This Agreement sets out the general terms governing the supply relationship. Specific quantities, prices, delivery dates, and quality specifications for individual orders shall be set out in written purchase orders issued by the Buyer and accepted by the Supplier, each of which shall incorporate the terms of this Agreement.
**3. TERM AND RENEWAL**

3.1 **Initial Term.** Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, the term of this Agreement shall commence on the Commencement Date and shall continue in full force and effect until 28 February 2025 (the "End Date"), unless earlier terminated in accordance with the provisions of Clause 16 (Termination) or extended in accordance with Clause 3.3 below. The Supply Contract LKC-2024-018 specifies its end_date as 2025-02-28. Record status: current.

3.2 **Expiration.** Upon the expiration of the term set out in Clause 3.1, this Agreement shall automatically terminate without the need for any further notice from either Party, and neither Party shall have any obligation to continue to supply or purchase the Goods thereafter, except for obligations that expressly survive termination pursuant to Clause 17 (Survival).

3.3 **Renewal Option.** The Buyer may, in its sole discretion, elect to renew this Agreement for a further period of twelve (12) months (the "Renewal Term") by delivering written notice of such election to the Supplier at least sixty (60) days prior to the End Date. Such notice shall specify the proposed renewal terms, including any adjustments to the prices set out in Schedule B.

3.4 **Negotiation of Renewal Terms.** Upon receipt of a renewal notice pursuant to Clause 3.3, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith the terms of the Renewal Term, including but not limited to pricing, delivery schedules, and any amendments to the Goods list. For the avoidance of doubt, the Supplier shall not be obligated to accept the Buyer's proposed renewal terms, and the Parties may agree to vary the scope of the Goods or the pricing structure during such negotiations.

3.5 **Failure to Agree.** If the Parties fail to reach agreement on the terms of a Renewal Term within thirty (30) days of the date of the Buyer's renewal notice, this Agreement shall terminate on the End Date in accordance with Clause 3.2, unless the Parties otherwise agree in writing to extend the negotiation period.

3.6 **Non-Renewal Notice.** If the Buyer elects not to renew this Agreement pursuant to Clause 3.3, or if the Buyer fails to deliver a renewal notice within the time period prescribed in Clause 3.3, this Agreement shall automatically terminate on the End Date. The Buyer shall have no further obligation to purchase Goods from the Supplier, and the Supplier shall have no further obligation to supply Goods to the Buyer, subject to the provisions of Clause 17 (Survival).

3.7 **Effect of Expiration or Termination.** Upon the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason: (a) the Buyer shall pay the Supplier for all Goods delivered and accepted prior to the date of such expiration or termination, in accordance with Clause 9 (Payment Terms); (b) the Supplier shall promptly return to the Buyer any materials, documents, or other property of the Buyer in its possession or control; and (c) each Party shall, to the extent permitted by law, return or destroy any confidential information of the other Party in its possession, in accordance with Clause 12 (Confidentiality).

3.8 **No Automatic Renewal.** For the avoidance of doubt, this Agreement shall not renew automatically. Any renewal shall be effective only upon the execution of a written renewal agreement or amendment signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. The Parties acknowledge that any extension of this Agreement beyond the End Date shall be subject to the mutual written consent of both Parties, and no course of dealing, performance, or acceptance of purchase orders after the End Date shall be deemed to constitute a renewal or extension of this Agreement.

3.9 **Notice Periods.** Any notice required to be given under this Clause 3 shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given if delivered personally, sent by courier, or sent by registered post or email, to the address of the receiving Party set out in Clause 18 (Notices), or to such other address as a Party may notify to the other in writing from time to time.
4.3 **Purchase Order Confirmation.** Upon receipt of a Purchase Order, the Supplier shall, within one (1) business day, confirm in writing (by email or other electronic means) its acceptance of the Purchase Order, including the quantities, delivery date, and delivery location specified therein. If the Supplier does not provide such confirmation within the prescribed period, the Purchase Order shall be deemed accepted by the Supplier, subject to the terms of this Agreement.

4.6 **Partial Deliveries.** The Supplier may make partial deliveries of a Purchase Order only with the Buyer's prior written consent. Where partial deliveries are permitted, the Supplier shall deliver each instalment in accordance with the delivery schedule set out in the Purchase Order, and the standard lead time in Clause 4.2 shall apply to each instalment separately. The Buyer shall not be obliged to accept partial deliveries made without prior written consent, and any such unauthorised partial delivery may be rejected by the Buyer in its entirety.

4.7 **Early Delivery.** The Buyer may, at its discretion, accept delivery of Goods before the scheduled delivery date. Early delivery shall not entitle the Supplier to earlier payment, and the Buyer shall have no obligation to store Goods delivered early. Where the Buyer accepts early delivery, risk in the Goods shall pass to the Buyer upon delivery, but title shall not pass until payment in accordance with Clause 9 (Payment Terms).

4.8 **Delivery Delays.** If the Supplier anticipates that it will be unable to deliver any Goods within the standard lead time set out in Clause 4.2, the Supplier shall notify the Buyer in writing as soon as reasonably practicable, and in any event no later than the end of the second (2nd) business day after the relevant Purchase Order is submitted. Such notification shall include the reason for the anticipated delay and the expected revised delivery date. For the avoidance of doubt, the Supplier's obligation to deliver within the standard lead time is absolute, and the Supplier shall not be excused from performance by reason of internal scheduling, procurement of raw materials, or staffing constraints, except where such failure arises from a Force Majeure Event as defined in Clause 16 (Force Majeure).

4.9 **Delivery during Public Holidays.** The Parties acknowledge that public holidays, including but not limited to Sallah and Christmas, may affect delivery schedules. Where a scheduled delivery date falls on a public holiday, the delivery shall be made on the next business day following such holiday, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties. The standard lead time set out in Clause 4.2 shall be extended by the number of days of the public holiday for the purposes of calculating the delivery date.

4.10 **Delivery Location and Access.** The Buyer shall provide the Supplier with reasonable access to its delivery points during normal business hours. The Buyer shall ensure that its premises are available to receive deliveries and that a duly authorised representative is present to accept and inspect the Goods upon delivery. If the Supplier is unable to complete a delivery due to the Buyer's failure to provide access or a representative, the Supplier shall not be liable for any delay resulting therefrom, and the delivery lead time shall be extended accordingly.

4.11 **Risk and Title.** Risk in the Goods shall pass to the Buyer upon delivery and acceptance of the Goods in accordance with this Clause 4. Title to the Goods shall pass to the Buyer upon the earlier of: (a) payment in full for the relevant Goods; or (b) delivery and acceptance of the Goods, provided that the Supplier may retain title to the Goods until payment in full is received, in accordance with Clause 9 (Payment Terms).
5. **PENALTIES FOR LATE DELIVERY**

5.1 **General Principle.** The Supplier acknowledges that timely delivery of the Goods is of the essence of this Contract. Where the Supplier fails to deliver the Goods, or any instalment thereof, by the delivery date set out in the relevant Purchase Order (as extended in accordance with Clause 4.9 or 4.10, as applicable), the Supplier shall be liable to pay to the Buyer liquidated damages in accordance with this Clause 5, unless the delay arises from a Force Majeure Event as defined in Clause 16 (Force Majeure).

5.2 **Rate of Penalty.** The penalty rate per day shall be 0.02 (two percent) of the value of the delayed Goods. For the avoidance of doubt, the penalty shall be calculated on the contract price of the Goods that are actually delivered late, and not on the aggregate value of all Goods under the relevant Purchase Order or this Contract. The Supply Contract LKC-2024-018 sets penalty_rate_per_day at 0.02. Record status: current. The penalty shall accrue on a daily basis for each day (or part thereof) that the Goods remain undelivered after the delivery date, subject to the cap set out in Clause 5.4 below.

5.3 **Calculation Method.** The penalty shall be calculated as follows:

    P = (V × R × D)

    where:
    - P is the total penalty payable;
    - V is the value of the delayed Goods (excluding any applicable taxes);
    - R is the penalty rate per day, being 0.02; and
    - D is the number of days (or part thereof) by which delivery is delayed.

    By way of illustration only, if the value of the delayed Goods is ₦500,000 and the delivery is delayed by three (3) days, the penalty shall be ₦30,000 (i.e., ₦500,000 × 0.02 × 3).

5.4 **Cap on Penalty.** The aggregate penalty payable under this Clause 5 shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the value of the delayed Goods. Once the penalty reaches the cap, the Buyer may, at its sole discretion, exercise its rights under Clause 5.5 or any other rights available to it under this Contract or at law.

5.5 **Buyer's Remedies Upon Continued Delay.** If the Supplier fails to deliver the Goods within fourteen (14) days after the delivery date, the Buyer may, by written notice to the Supplier:
    (a) terminate the relevant Purchase Order in respect of the delayed Goods without liability on the part of the Buyer; and/or
    (b) procure substitute Goods from a third party, and the Supplier shall be liable for any additional costs incurred by the Buyer in procuring such substitute Goods, less any penalty already paid or deducted under this Clause 5.

5.6 **Set-Off.** The Buyer may deduct any penalty payable under this Clause 5 from any amounts owing to the Supplier under this Contract or any other agreement between the Parties. If the amounts owing are insufficient to cover the penalty, the Supplier shall pay the shortfall to the Buyer within fourteen (14) days of receipt of an invoice therefor.

5.7 **Exclusive Remedy.** Save in the case of fraud, wilful default, or gross negligence, the penalties set out in this Clause 5 shall be the Buyer's sole and exclusive remedy for any delay in delivery of the Goods, and the Buyer shall not be entitled to claim any further damages, compensation, or other remedy in respect of such delay.

5.8 **No Waiver.** The exercise by the Buyer of any right under this Clause 5 shall not be deemed a waiver of any other right or remedy available to it under this Contract or at law. Any delay or failure by the Buyer to exercise any such right shall not operate as a waiver thereof.

5.9 **Notification of Delay.** The Supplier shall notify the Buyer in writing immediately upon becoming aware that it will be unable to deliver the Goods by the delivery date. Such notification shall include the reason for the anticipated delay and the expected revised delivery date. The Supplier shall provide the Buyer with regular updates on the status of the delayed delivery until the Goods are delivered. The provision of such notification shall not relieve the Supplier of its obligations under this Clause 5.
**6. QUALITY AND INSPECTION**

6.1 **Quality Standards.** The Supplier warrants that all Goods supplied under this Contract shall:
(a) conform to the specifications, descriptions, samples, and quality standards set out in the relevant Purchase Order and in the Technical Specifications annexed hereto as Annex B, as may be updated from time to time by written agreement of the Parties;
(b) be of merchantable quality, fresh, fit for the purpose for which goods of that kind are ordinarily used, and free from defects in material and workmanship;
(c) comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and standards in force in the Federal Republic of Nigeria, including but not limited to the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) requirements, the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) requirements, and any municipal health and safety regulations applicable to the delivery location;
(d) not be adulterated, misbranded, or falsely described, and shall be properly labelled with the country of origin, production date, best-before date, and any other information required by law; and
(e) where the Goods are perishable, be produced, handled, stored, and transported in accordance with good manufacturing and cold-chain practices, as applicable, so as to ensure that the Goods remain within the required temperature range from the point of production to the point of delivery.

6.2 **Inspection and Testing.** The Buyer, its agents, or its designated third-party inspectors shall have the right, at all reasonable times, to inspect, test, and sample the Goods, and to inspect the Supplier's production, storage, and handling facilities, during normal business hours and upon reasonable prior notice. Such inspection may occur:
(a) at the point of production or packing;
(b) during transit, where reasonably practicable;
(c) at the point of delivery; and
(d) at any other stage in the supply chain as the Buyer may reasonably require.

The Buyer shall provide the Supplier with at least forty-eight (48) hours' written notice of any inspection other than at the point of delivery, unless the inspection is in response to a suspected quality or safety issue, in which case the Buyer may conduct the inspection with shorter notice or without notice if required to protect public health.

6.3 **Cost of Inspection.** The cost of the initial inspection and testing of the Goods shall be borne by the Supplier, provided that such inspection is conducted in accordance with this Clause 6. If the Goods are found to conform to the Contract, the cost of any subsequent or repeat inspection shall be borne by the Buyer. If the Goods are found not to conform, the cost of the initial and any repeat inspection shall be borne by the Supplier, and the Supplier shall reimburse the Buyer for any reasonable costs incurred by the Buyer in connection with such inspection within fourteen (14) days of receipt of an invoice therefor.

6.4 **Right to Reject.** The Buyer may reject any Goods that do not conform to the Contract, in whole or in part, by giving written notice to the Supplier within a reasonable time after delivery or after the defect is or ought to have been discovered. Such notice shall specify the reason for rejection. Where the rejection is for a defect that is not apparent on reasonable inspection at the time of delivery, the Buyer shall notify the Supplier within a reasonable time after such defect is discovered, and in any event no later than five (5) days after the relevant best-before date or, for non-perishable Goods, within thirty (30) days of delivery.

Upon rejection, the Buyer shall, at the Supplier's option and cost, either:
(a) return the rejected Goods to the Supplier; or
(b) dispose of the rejected Goods in a safe and lawful manner, and the Supplier shall reimburse the Buyer for any reasonable disposal costs.

(b) the delivery note number(s) and date(s) of delivery;

(e) the Supplier's VAT registration number and a valid Tax Identification Number (TIN); and
(f) such other information as the Buyer may reasonably require from time to time.

7.3 **Disputed Invoices.** If any portion of an invoice is disputed in good faith, the Buyer shall notify the Supplier in writing within ten (10) days of receipt of the invoice, specifying the nature and extent of the dispute. The undisputed portion of the invoice shall be paid in accordance with Clause 7.1, and the disputed portion shall be resolved in accordance with Clause 12 (Dispute Resolution). A disputed invoice shall not constitute a waiver of any rights of the Buyer under this Contract, nor shall it relieve the Supplier of any of its obligations.

7.4 **Late Payment.** Without prejudice to any other rights or remedies available to the Supplier, if the Buyer fails to pay any undisputed amount by the due date, the Supplier shall be entitled to charge interest on the overdue amount at a rate of two percent (2%) per annum above the Central Bank of Nigeria's prevailing Monetary Policy Rate, calculated on a daily basis from the due date until the date of actual payment. 7.6 **Taxes and Duties.** All prices are exclusive of VAT and other applicable taxes, which shall be added at the prevailing rate at the time of invoicing. The Supplier shall be responsible for all taxes, duties, levies, and charges imposed on the Goods or on the Supplier in connection with the performance of this Contract, except for taxes imposed on the Buyer's income. Where the Buyer is required by law to withhold any tax from payments, the Buyer shall make the withholding and provide the Supplier with a withholding tax credit note or certificate within a reasonable time.

8.2 **Duty to Notify.** A Party affected by Force Majeure shall, as soon as reasonably practicable (and in any event within seven (7) days of the onset of the Force Majeure event), notify the other Party in writing of the nature and expected duration of the event, the obligations affected, and the steps being taken to mitigate its impact. **4.0 OPENING REMARKS**

Mr. Emeka Okafor welcomed all attendees and thanked them for making time despite busy schedules. He noted that the meeting was a continuation of discussions that began informally in September 2024, and that today’s session was meant to formalise the negotiation process. He stressed the importance of arriving at a mutually beneficial agreement before the end of the year, given that the current contract expires on 31 December 2024.

He reminded participants that the company operates a total of 12 outlets — 7 in Lagos, 3 in Abuja, 1 in Port Harcourt, and 1 in Ibadan — and that any changes to supply or staffing arrangements must be scalable across all locations. He also mentioned that the company had recently opened a new outlet in Lekki (Outlet 12) and that staffing requirements were still being finalised for that location.

---

**5.0 REVIEW OF CURRENT SUPPLY CONTRACT**

A summary of the current contract was presented by Mrs. Folake Adeyemi. Key points included:

- The current contract with FreshLink Foods & Supplies Ltd. covers the supply of fresh produce, frozen items, dry goods, and cleaning supplies.
- The contract value for 2024 was ₦85,000,000 (Eighty-Five Million Naira), with quarterly reviews.
- Delivery schedules were set for Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays for Lagos outlets; Tuesdays and Thursdays for Abuja; and weekly (Saturdays) for Port Harcourt and Ibadan.
- The contract includes a penalty clause for late deliveries exceeding 24 hours, except in cases of force majeure.
Mr. Bakare explained that the flat discount would be easier for both parties to administer, as it avoided the need for quarterly reconciliations and potential disputes over tier classification. He also noted that FreshLink had absorbed significant cost increases in logistics and fuel during 2024, and that the proposed structure reflected a genuine effort to share the benefits of scale without undermining their own viability.

Mrs. Adeyemi asked for clarification on how the 4.5% discount would be applied to invoices. Mr. Bakare confirmed that the discount would be applied at the point of invoicing, on a line-item basis, rather than as a year-end rebate. This, he said, would improve the company's cash flow and reduce the administrative burden on both finance teams.

**8.0 NEGOTIATION ON THRESHOLDS AND EXCLUSIONS**

A lengthy discussion followed regarding the ₦10,000,000 exclusion threshold. Mr. Okafor argued that the exclusion unfairly penalised the smaller outlets in Port Harcourt and Ibadan, which had lower volumes but were still essential to the company's national presence. He proposed that the exclusion be reduced to ₦7,500,000, or that the discount be calculated on a per-outlet basis rather than on the consolidated contract.

Mr. Bakare resisted the per-outlet approach, stating that FreshLink's cost savings were derived from consolidated logistics and bulk purchasing, not from individual outlet volumes. He conceded, however, that the exclusion threshold could be reviewed after the first quarter of 2025, based on actual consumption data. He also agreed to include a clause that would allow for a joint review of the discount structure if the company's total annual spend exceeded ₦100,000,000.

The discussion then turned to the treatment of cleaning supplies and dry goods. Mrs. Adeyemi noted that these categories had lower margins and were often subject to separate pricing arrangements. It was agreed that the volume discount would apply only to fresh produce and frozen items, which constituted approximately 78% of the company's procurement spend. Dry goods and cleaning supplies would remain under the existing pricing schedule, with a separate 2% prompt-payment discount for invoices settled within 7 days.

**9.0 AGREED TERMS ON VOLUME DISCOUNT**

After further deliberation, the parties reached a consensus on the following terms, which were recorded as the official outcome of this negotiation session:

- **Volume discount:** FreshLink shall apply a flat 4.5% discount on the invoiced value of fresh produce and frozen items supplied under the new contract, effective 1 January 2025.
- **Minimum commitment:** The company commits to a minimum annual purchase of ₦90,000,000 across all categories.
- **Quarterly incentive:** An additional 1% discount shall apply to any quarter in which fresh produce and frozen item spend exceeds ₦24,000,000. This discount shall be applied to that quarter's invoices within 15 days of the quarter-end reconciliation.
- **Exclusion:** The first ₦10,000,000 of annual spend shall not be subject to the discount. This exclusion shall be reviewed after Q1 2025.
- **Scope:** The discount applies only to fresh produce and frozen items. Dry goods and cleaning supplies are excluded, but retain a 2% prompt-payment discount for settlement within 7 days of invoice.
- **Review clause:** Both parties agree to a joint review of the discount structure should annual spend exceed ₦100,000,000.

The Negotiation Note NN-2024-11 concluded with outcome agreed on volume discount. Record status: current.

**12.0 MEETING OF 12 FEBRUARY 2024 – SUPPLIER: TROPICAL FOODS LIMITED**

**Attendees:** Mrs. Folake Adeyemi (Procurement Manager), Mr. Emeka Okafor (Head of Supply Chain), Mr. Ibrahim Suleiman (Managing Director, Tropical Foods), Ms. Ngozi Eze (Sales Representative, Tropical Foods)

**Agenda:** Review of price escalation clause for palm oil and vegetable oil; delivery schedule for Ramadan period.

**Discussion Summary:**

Mr. Suleiman opened the meeting by restating Tropical Foods' request for a price adjustment clause tied to the international commodity index. He noted that crude palm oil prices had risen 14% since the last quarter and that his company could not absorb further increases without revising the current fixed-price agreement.

Mrs. Adeyemi responded that the existing contract, signed in March 2023, already contained a semi-annual review mechanism. She pointed out that the next review was scheduled for 1 April 2024, and that any adjustment would be applied prospectively, not retroactively. Mr. Okafor supported this position, adding that the company's budget cycle for the second half of the year had been approved based on the current price list.

After discussion, the following points were agreed:

- The April review will consider the international commodity index published by the Malaysian Palm Oil Council, with a tolerance band of ±5% before any price change is triggered.
- Any adjustment will be capped at 8% per review period.
- Tropical Foods will provide supporting documentation for any requested increase at least 14 days before the review date.
- Delivery frequency during Ramadan will be increased from twice weekly to three times weekly, with no change to the existing delivery charges.

**Action Items:**

- Mr. Suleiman to submit the commodity index data and supporting invoices by 15 March 2024.
- Ms. Eze to circulate the revised Ramadan delivery schedule by 20 February 2024.
- Mrs. Adeyemi to prepare a brief on the price adjustment mechanism for the next review meeting.

The Negotiation Note NN-2024-02 concluded with agreement on the review mechanism and Ramadan schedule. Record status: current.

**Agenda:** Bottled water supply for the 2024 dry season; possible rebranding of table water; logistics for the Sallah break.

**Discussion Summary:**

Mr. Bakare presented Northbridge's proposal to supply 500ml and 1.5L bottled water at ₦1,150 and ₦2,050 per carton respectively, representing a 6% increase from the 2023 rates. He attributed the increase to higher PET resin costs and diesel price movements.

Mrs. Adeyemi noted that the company's current supplier had offered a smaller increase of 3.5% and asked Northbridge to reconsider. Mr. Bakare stated that Northbridge could not match that figure but offered a 4% increase if the company agreed to a minimum monthly offtake of 1,200 cartons. Ms. Obi added that Northbridge would provide branded display racks at no cost for the company's two flagship outlets.

Mr. Okafor asked about delivery lead times during the Sallah break. Mr. Bakare confirmed that Northbridge would maintain a delivery on the Tuesday before Sallah and resume on the second working day after the holiday. No premium would be charged for these deliveries.

**Agreed Points:**

- Price increase of 4% on bottled water, effective 1 May 2024, subject to a minimum monthly offtake of 1,200 cartons.
- Northbridge to supply 60 branded display racks, delivered in two batches of 30.
- The company may exit the arrangement with 60 days' written notice if the minimum offtake is not met due to reduced customer demand.

The penalty shall accrue on a daily basis for each day (or part thereof) that the Goods remain undelivered after the delivery date, subject to the cap set out in Clause 5.4 below.

5.3 **Calculation Method.** The penalty shall be calculated as follows:

    P = (V × R × D)

    where:
    - P is the total penalty payable;
    - V is the value of the delayed Goods (excluding any applicable taxes);
    - R is the penalty rate per day, being 0.02; and
    - D is the number of days (or part thereof) by which delivery is delayed.

    By way of illustration only, if the value of the delayed Goods is ₦500,000 and the delivery is delayed by three (3) days, the penalty shall be ₦30,000 (i.e., ₦500,000 × 0.02 × 3).

5.4 **Cap on Penalty.** The aggregate penalty payable under this Clause 5 shall not exceed ten percent (10%) of the value of the delayed Goods. Once the penalty reaches the cap, the Buyer may, at its sole discretion, exercise its rights under Clause 5.5 or any other rights available to it under this Contract or at law.

5.5 **Buyer's Remedies Upon Continued Delay.** If the Supplier fails to deliver the Goods within fourteen (14) days after the delivery date, the Buyer may, by written notice to the Supplier:
    (a) terminate the relevant Purchase Order in respect of the delayed Goods without liability on the part of the Buyer; and/or
    (b) procure substitute Goods from a third party, and the Supplier shall be liable for any additional costs incurred by the Buyer in procuring such substitute Goods, less any penalty already paid or deducted under this Clause 5.

5.6 **Set-Off.** The Buyer may deduct any penalty payable under this Clause 5 from any amounts owing to the Supplier under this Contract or any other agreement between the Parties. If the amounts owing are insufficient to cover the penalty, the Supplier shall pay the shortfall to the Buyer within fourteen (14) days of receipt of an invoice therefor.

5.7 **Exclusive Remedy.** Save in the case of fraud, wilful default, or gross negligence, the penalties set out in this Clause 5 shall be the Buyer's sole and exclusive remedy for any delay in delivery of the Goods, and the Buyer shall not be entitled to claim any further damages, compensation, or other remedy in respect of such delay.

5.8 **No Waiver.** The exercise by the Buyer of any right under this Clause 5 shall not be deemed a waiver of any other right or remedy available to it under this Contract or at law. Any delay or failure by the Buyer to exercise any such right shall not operate as a waiver thereof.

5.9 **Notification of Delay.** The Supplier shall notify the Buyer in writing immediately upon becoming aware that it will be unable to deliver the Goods by the delivery date. Such notification shall include the reason for the anticipated delay and the expected revised delivery date. The Supplier shall provide the Buyer with regular updates on the status of the delayed delivery until the Goods are delivered. The provision of such notification shall not relieve the Supplier of its obligations under this Clause 5.

**6. QUALITY AND INSPECTION**

6.1 **Quality Standards.** The Supplier warrants that all Goods supplied under this Contract shall:
(a) conform to the specifications, descriptions, samples, and quality standards set out in the relevant Purchase Order and in the Technical Specifications annexed hereto as Annex B, as may be updated from time to time by written agreement of the Parties;
(b) be of merchantable quality, fresh, fit for the purpose for which goods of that kind are ordinarily used, and free from defects in material and workmanship;
(c) comply with all applicable laws, regulations, and standards in force in the Federal Republic of Nigeria, including but not limited to the National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) requirements, the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON) requirements, and any municipal health and safety regulations applicable to the delivery location;
(d) not be adulterated, misbranded, or falsely described, and shall be properly labelled with the country of origin, production date, best-before date, and any other information required by law; and
(e) where the Goods are perishable, be produced, handled, stored, and transported in accordance with good manufacturing and cold-chain practices, as applicable, so as to ensure that the Goods remain within the required temperature range from the point of production to the point of delivery.

6.2 **Inspection and Testing.** The Buyer, its agents, or its designated third-party inspectors shall have the right, at all reasonable times, to inspect, test, and sample the Goods, and to inspect the Supplier's production, storage, and handling facilities, during normal business hours and upon reasonable prior notice. Such inspection may occur:
(a) at the point of production or packing;
(b) during transit, where reasonably practicable;
(c) at the point of delivery; and
(d) at any other stage in the supply chain as the Buyer may reasonably require.

The Buyer shall provide the Supplier with at least forty-eight (48) hours' written notice of any inspection other than at the point of delivery, unless the inspection is in response to a suspected quality or safety issue, in which case the Buyer may conduct the inspection with shorter notice or without notice if required to protect public health.

6.3 **Cost of Inspection.** The cost of the initial inspection and testing of the Goods shall be borne by the Supplier, provided that such inspection is conducted in accordance with this Clause 6. If the Goods are found to conform to the Contract, the cost of any subsequent or repeat inspection shall be borne by the Buyer. If the Goods are found not to conform, the cost of the initial and any repeat inspection shall be borne by the Supplier, and the Supplier shall reimburse the Buyer for any reasonable costs incurred by the Buyer in connection with such inspection within fourteen (14) days of receipt of an invoice therefor.

6.4 **Right to Reject.** The Buyer may reject any Goods that do not conform to the Contract, in whole or in part, by giving written notice to the Supplier within a reasonable time after delivery or after the defect is or ought to have been discovered. Such notice shall specify the reason for rejection. Where the rejection is for a defect that is not apparent on reasonable inspection at the time of delivery, the Buyer shall notify the Supplier within a reasonable time after such defect is discovered, and in any event no later than five (5) days after the relevant best-before date or, for non-perishable Goods, within thirty (30) days of delivery.

Upon rejection, the Buyer shall, at the Supplier's option and cost, either:
(a) return the rejected Goods to the Supplier; or
(b) dispose of the rejected Goods in a safe and lawful manner, and the Supplier shall reimburse the Buyer for any reasonable disposal costs.

- The contract value for 2024 was ₦85,000,000 (Eighty-Five Million Naira), with quarterly reviews.

documents.content:
Mr. Bakare explained that the flat discount would be easier for both parties to administer, as it avoided the need for quarterly reconciliations and potential disputes over tier classification. He also noted that FreshLink had absorbed significant cost increases in logistics and fuel during 2024, and that the proposed structure reflected a genuine effort to share the benefits of scale without undermining their own viability.

Mrs. Adeyemi asked for clarification on how the 4.5% discount would be applied to invoices. Mr. Bakare confirmed that the discount would be applied at the point of invoicing, on a line-item basis, rather than as a year-end rebate. This, he said, would improve the company's cash flow and reduce the administrative burden on both finance teams.

**8.0 NEGOTIATION ON THRESHOLDS AND EXCLUSIONS**

A lengthy discussion followed regarding the ₦10,000,000 exclusion threshold. Mr. Okafor argued that the exclusion unfairly penalised the smaller outlets in Port Harcourt and Ibadan, which had lower volumes but were still essential to the company's national presence. He proposed that the exclusion be reduced to ₦7,500,000, or that the discount be calculated on a per-outlet basis rather than on the consolidated contract.

Mr. Bakare resisted the per-outlet approach, stating that FreshLink's cost savings were derived from consolidated logistics and bulk purchasing, not from individual outlet volumes. He conceded, however, that the exclusion threshold could be reviewed after the first quarter of 2025, based on actual consumption data. He also agreed to include a clause that would allow for a joint review of the discount structure if the company's total annual spend exceeded ₦100,000,000.

The discussion then turned to the treatment of cleaning supplies and dry goods. Mrs. Adeyemi noted that these categories had lower margins and were often subject to separate pricing arrangements. It was agreed that the volume discount would apply only to fresh produce and frozen items, which constituted approximately 78% of the company's procurement spend. Dry goods and cleaning supplies would remain under the existing pricing schedule, with a separate 2% prompt-payment discount for invoices settled within 7 days.

**9.0 AGREED TERMS ON VOLUME DISCOUNT**

After further deliberation, the parties reached a consensus on the following terms, which were recorded as the official outcome of this negotiation session:

- **Volume discount:** FreshLink shall apply a flat 4.5% discount on the invoiced value of fresh produce and frozen items supplied under the new contract, effective 1 January 2025.
- **Minimum commitment:** The company commits to a minimum annual purchase of ₦90,000,000 across all categories.
- **Quarterly incentive:** An additional 1% discount shall apply to any quarter in which fresh produce and frozen item spend exceeds ₦24,000,000. This discount shall be applied to that quarter's invoices within 15 days of the quarter-end reconciliation.
- **Exclusion:** The first ₦10,000,000 of annual spend shall not be subject to the discount. This exclusion shall be reviewed after Q1 2025.
- **Scope:** The discount applies only to fresh produce and frozen items. Dry goods and cleaning supplies are excluded, but retain a 2% prompt-payment discount for settlement within 7 days of invoice.
- **Review clause:** Both parties agree to a joint review of the discount structure should annual spend exceed ₦100,000,000.

The Negotiation Note NN-2024-11 concluded with outcome agreed on volume discount. Record status: current.

**10.0 ACTION ITEMS**

- Mrs. Folake Adeyemi to prepare a draft addendum to the existing contract reflecting the agreed volume discount terms, for review by Mr. Emeka Okafor and the legal team.

**12.0 MEETING OF 12 FEBRUARY 2024 – SUPPLIER: TROPICAL FOODS LIMITED**

**Attendees:** Mrs. Folake Adeyemi (Procurement Manager), Mr. Emeka Okafor (Head of Supply Chain), Mr. Ibrahim Suleiman (Managing Director, Tropical Foods), Ms. Ngozi Eze (Sales Representative, Tropical Foods)

**Agenda:** Review of price escalation clause for palm oil and vegetable oil; delivery schedule for Ramadan period.

**Discussion Summary:**

Mr. Suleiman opened the meeting by restating Tropical Foods' request for a price adjustment clause tied to the international commodity index. He noted that crude palm oil prices had risen 14% since the last quarter and that his company could not absorb further increases without revising the current fixed-price agreement.

Mrs. Adeyemi responded that the existing contract, signed in March 2023, already contained a semi-annual review mechanism. She pointed out that the next review was scheduled for 1 April 2024, and that any adjustment would be applied prospectively, not retroactively. Mr. Okafor supported this position, adding that the company's budget cycle for the second half of the year had been approved based on the current price list.

After discussion, the following points were agreed:

- The April review will consider the international commodity index published by the Malaysian Palm Oil Council, with a tolerance band of ±5% before any price change is triggered.
- Any adjustment will be capped at 8% per review period.
- Tropical Foods will provide supporting documentation for any requested increase at least 14 days before the review date.
- Delivery frequency during Ramadan will be increased from twice weekly to three times weekly, with no change to the existing delivery charges.

**Action Items:**

- Mr. Suleiman to submit the commodity index data and supporting invoices by 15 March 2024.
- Ms. Eze to circulate the revised Ramadan delivery schedule by 20 February 2024.
- Mrs. Adeyemi to prepare a brief on the price adjustment mechanism for the next review meeting.

The Negotiation Note NN-2024-02 concluded with agreement on the review mechanism and Ramadan schedule. Record status: current.

**13.0 MEETING OF 9 APRIL 2024 – SUPPLIER: NORTHBRIDGE BEVERAGES & PACKAGING**

**Attendees:** Mrs. Folake Adeyemi, Mr. Emeka Okafor, Mr. Tunde Bakare (Regional Sales Manager, Northbridge), Ms. Chiamaka Obi (Key Accounts Officer, Northbridge)

**Agenda:** Bottled water supply for the 2024 dry season; possible rebranding of table water; logistics for the Sallah break.

**Discussion Summary:**

Mr. Bakare presented Northbridge's proposal to supply 500ml and 1.5L bottled water at ₦1,150 and ₦2,050 per carton respectively, representing a 6% increase from the 2023 rates. He attributed the increase to higher PET resin costs and diesel price movements.

Mrs. Adeyemi noted that the company's current supplier had offered a smaller increase of 3.5% and asked Northbridge to reconsider. Mr. Bakare stated that Northbridge could not match that figure but offered a 4% increase if the company agreed to a minimum monthly offtake of 1,200 cartons. Ms. Obi added that Northbridge would provide branded display racks at no cost for the company's two flagship outlets.

Mr. Okafor asked about delivery lead times during the Sallah break. Mr. Bakare confirmed that Northbridge would maintain a delivery on the Tuesday before Sallah and resume on the second working day after the holiday. No premium would be charged for these deliveries.

**Agreed Points:**

- Price increase of 4% on bottled water, effective 1 May 2024, subject to a minimum monthly offtake of 1,200 cartons.
- Northbridge to supply 60 branded display racks, delivered in two batches of 30.
- The company may exit the arrangement with 60 days' written notice if the minimum offtake is not met due to reduced customer demand.
